entries.title: Thick-point optimization restates the unknown LQG dimension
entries.statement: For 0<gamma<2, xi>0, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2, and alpha in [-2,2], set F(alpha)=(2-alpha^2/2)/(xi*(Q-alpha)). Then Q-alpha>0 and gamma/xi-F(alpha)=(alpha-gamma)^2/(2*xi*(Q-alpha)); the unique maximum is gamma/xi at alpha=gamma. In the LQG parametrization xi=gamma/d_gamma, maximizing F returns d_gamma and does not evaluate xi. Gwynne--Pfeffer Theorem 1.5 gives this profile for each fixed alpha and a deterministic or field-independent full-Euclidean-dimension Borel set; the algebra alone does not create one probability-one event for all alpha or an uncountable-union dimension rule. The endpoint gamma=2 is excluded.
assumptions: only deterministic profile algebra is asserted; published thick-point theorem is fixed-alpha almost surely

entries.title: Snowflaking preserves reduced scaling while changing dimension
entries.statement: For any metric D on X and 0<a<1, D^a is a metric with the same topology and dim_H(X,D^a)=dim_H(X,D)/a. If D_{h+c}=exp(xi*c)D_h for constant c, then D_{h+c}^a=exp(a*xi*c)D_h^a, so the product xi*dim_H is unchanged. This shows that constant-shift covariance alone cannot determine metric dimension. It is not a second LQG metric: every continuous path from 0 to 1 in the snowflaked Euclidean interval has infinite D^a-length, by the first hitting times of levels k/n and partition sums n^(1-a). Thus the LQG length-space and pathwise Weyl axioms are outside this countermodel.
assumptions: only reduced constant-shift covariance is tested, not full strong-LQG axioms

relations.rationale: The profile card says maximizing F returns gamma/xi without evaluating xi. The existing P0297 card asks to determine d_gamma for general gamma, and xi=gamma/d_gamma. The primary theorem supplies the profile; this link records why it does not solve the problem.

The snowflake card says constant-shift covariance alone cannot determine dimension. The existing attempt card says xi*d=gamma does not calculate xi. The covering construction reproduces the reason for that limitation.

The snowflake card preserves xi*dimension while changing dimension under reduced scaling. The thick-point card maximizes to gamma/xi while leaving xi unevaluated. Both are distinct, independently checked obstructions to inferring an exact d_gamma from a restatement of xi*d_gamma=gamma.
